events.title: The Mac Dynasty retreated to Cao Bang
events.description: After falling at Thang Long to the Le - Trinh forces, the Mac Dynasty retreated to the land of Cao Bang to build citadels, establish royal power, and rule as a warlord state here for over 80 years (until 1677), creating special cultural and historical imprints.

events.title: Leader Nguyen Ai Quoc returned to the country
events.description: After 30 years of traveling abroad to find a way to save the country, leader Nguyen Ai Quoc crossed landmark 108 on the Vietnam - China border, returning to Pac Bo to directly lead the Vietnamese revolutionary movement.

events.title: Establishment of the Viet Minh Front
events.description: The 8th Conference of the Party Central Committee, chaired by Nguyen Ai Quoc at Khuoi Nam hut (Pac Bo), decided to establish the Vietnam Independence League (Viet Minh for short) to unite the entire nation to fight the French and expel the Japanese.

events.title: Establishment of the Vietnam Propaganda Liberation Army
events.description: In the Tran Hung Dao forest, the Vietnam Propaganda Liberation Army (the predecessor of the People's Army of Vietnam) was established with 34 soldiers, commanded by Comrade Vo Nguyen Giap, implementing the motto 'Politics is more important than military'.

events.title: Phai Khat - Na Ngan Victory
events.description: Immediately after its establishment, the Vietnam Propaganda Liberation Army disguised themselves, used tactics to ambush and completely destroy the two posts of Phai Khat and Na Ngan, initiating the tradition of 'winning the first battle' of our army.

events.title: Seizing power in Cao Bang Town
events.description: The Uprising Committee of Cao Bang Province led the masses and armed forces into the town, seizing the Governor's Palace and the civil guard post. The provisional revolutionary government was established, abolishing the enemy's ruling apparatus.

events.title: Dong Khe Battle (Opening of the Border Campaign)
events.description: Our army opened fire to attack the Dong Khe outpost cluster. After 54 hours of fierce fighting, we completely destroyed this outpost, cutting an important link in the French defense line on Route 4, isolating Cao Bang.

events.title: Liberation of Cao Bang
events.description: After losing Dong Khe and suffering heavy losses in the disastrous retreat on Route 4 (the Charton and Le Page columns were wiped out), the French forces were forced to abandon Cao Bang Town. Cao Bang became the first province to be completely liberated.

events.title: Re-establishment of Cao Bang Province
events.description: The 4th Session of the 6th National Assembly issued a resolution to split Cao Lang Province (which had been merged since 1975) into two provinces, Cao Bang and Lang Son. Cao Bang Province returned to its former administrative boundaries.

events.title: Fighting to protect the northern border in Cao Bang
events.description: The Chinese army launched a massive attack on the Cao Bang border, heavily destroying Cao Bang Town and the Pac Bo relic site. The military and people of Cao Bang, especially at Bang Giang Bridge and the border high points, fought resiliently to stop the enemy's advance.
